chunks: And from him (Al-Shaykh) from Ibn Faddal from Yunus who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'When I enter the Ka'bah, what should I do?' He said, 'Take hold of the door rings when you enter the Ka'bah, then proceed until you reach the two pillars, and pray on the red marble. Then when you exit the House and descend the stairs, pray two rak'ahs to your right.'

key_terms.الرُّخَامَةُ الْحَمْرَاءُ: The red marble, a specific slab inside the Ka'bah where prayer is recommended.
key_terms.الْبَيْت: The House, a common title for the Ka'bah.
key_terms.الْعَمُودَيْنِ: The two pillars, referring to the pillars of the Ka'bah.
key_terms.الْكَعْبَة: The Ka'bah, the cubic building at the center of the Grand Mosque in Mecca.

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended ritual prayer and actions when entering and leaving the Ka'bah according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details the specific Sunnah of entering the Ka'bah, emphasizing the physical connection to the structure by holding the door rings and performing prayer on the red marble slab (Hajar al-Hamra) between the two pillars. It highlights the Ka'bah not merely as a directional marker but as a sacred space for direct worship, with the exit ritual reinforcing the sanctity of the site through additional voluntary prayers.
